_comment: Tharga.Team support integration — a Slack app manifest.
Slack issues tokens per workspace installation, so there is no Tharga-owned app to install: each
consumer creates their own. This manifest is what makes that a two-minute job rather than an
To use it: Slack API -> Your Apps -> Create New App -> From an app manifest, pick the workspace,
paste this file, then Install to Workspace. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...) into
Slack:BotToken and the Signing Secret into Slack:SigningSecret.
Then invite the bot to the channel: /invite @Tharga Support. It cannot post to a channel it is not in,
and it cannot read the member list of one either — which is how support presence is determined.
Replace YOUR-HOST below with the public address of your deployment. Slack cannot reach localhost, so
for local work use a tunnel (ngrok or similar) and update the request URL to match.
Every scope here is required by code in Tharga.Team.Support. If you remove one, the feature that
needs it stops working silently rather than loudly:
chat:write    -> chat.postMessage       posting notifications and case replies
users:read    -> users.getPresence      whether anybody on support is active
channels:read -> conversations.members  who is on a public support channel
groups:read   -> conversations.members  the same, for a private support channel
